speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These Parliamentary Questions (PQs) raise general issues concerning or affecting racial integration and various policies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Racial discrimination sows discord amongst and between different communities and threatens the harmony that we have worked so hard over so many generations to build up.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Our multi-racialism is not perfect and there is still much that we can do to improve.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, we have an enforcement and legal framework to deal with egregious cases that undermine our racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Under the Penal Code, it is an offence to commit acts that deliberately wound the racial and religious feelings of any person, that promote enmity between different racial and religious groups, or that are prejudicial to the maintenance of racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Government does not tolerate hate speech and will investigate anyone who sows enmity between races.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Just last year, an individual used a Twitter account to make racist remarks against people of different races.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, under the Broadcasting Act, IMDA can direct Internet Content Providers to take down broadcasting material that glorifies, incites or endorses ethnic, racial or religious hatred, strife or intolerance, which is prohibited under the Internet Code of Practice.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, Sir, we foster social norms for respectful online behaviour and discourse.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Recent events have highlighted the polarising effect of online platforms and social media, and we must guard against potential divisions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is especially important because we can only strengthen our multiculturalism, if we treat fellow Singaporeans as partners, instead of adversaries to be confronted.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To achieve this, we will require a whole-of-society partnership, with Government, industry and, of course, the community, and each of us collaborating.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, the Media Literacy Council (MLC) promotes responsible online behaviour by working with partners to support projects by our youth promoting the shared values of respect, responsibility, empathy and integrity; and online behaviours that demonstrate safety, responsibility and also civility.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Social media companies also play a part in managing content hosted on their platforms, by constantly improving and enforcing their policies to remove content that promotes violence against people based on race or ethnicity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, Facebook has a set of Community Standards, which classifies "Hate Speech" as "objectionable content".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Twitter also has a similar set of policies on hateful conduct.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Government works with these social media companies to promote healthy online discourse.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) also encourages ground-up projects that promote racial and religious harmony, including those that leverage digital and online platforms.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MCCY provides funding support through its Harmony Fund and partners community organisations to organise initiatives such as the Mission:Unite Hackathon in December 2020.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Third, we foster open, meaningful and responsible conversations on race and religion.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These conversations bring Singaporeans together to discuss and find common ground on issues important to us as a people, and in the process, build up mutual trust, respect and also understanding.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To support such dialogues and civic engagements, we work with stakeholders in the public, private and also people sectors to identify and equip individuals with the relevant skills, so that they can in turn create safe spaces for sensitive topics to be discussed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Within the Public Service, we have trained and developed a sizeable pool of facilitators who are able to design and lead engagements both within the Public Service and with the wider community.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: An example is the on-going Emerging Stronger Conversations, which I am sure many Members have heard or participated in, which are mostly led by public officers across different Government agencies who are trained in facilitation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Beyond the public service, community and religious groups also play a key role in encouraging constructive discussions, clarifying doubts and misconceptions, and rallying Singaporeans around our shared values to take a stand against divisive rhetoric on racial and religious issues.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Our religious and community leaders have amongst them, strong facilitation and convening capabilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example in June, MCCY supported the Centre For Interfaith Understanding's launch of a series of public workshops that aim to discover, develop and deepen interfaith facilitators' role and expose them to cross-cutting issues such as interfaith marriages and economic inequality when discussing race and religion.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, having other segments of society come together, discussing policies and economic policies as well, but having the undertone of race and religious harmony as a backdrop.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Last month, MCCY also launched the "Create and Connect" digital media workshops where 40 participants from religious and community organisations came together to learn from technology companies on how to impactfully engage audiences on sensitive race and religion issues, and also manage complex online discussions in a constructive manner.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MCCY also supports community-driven dialogues that provide safe spaces and opportunities for open dialogue and mutual learning.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, OnePeople.sg has been organising the "Regardless of Race" dialogue series since 2019, with its most recent sixth edition in April this year.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These dialogues address salient issues on racial harmony, including the impact of social media on race and religious relations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Fourth, Sir, we are committed to enlarging the common spaces in which all Singaporeans can live, work and play together, and also share the daily lived experiences that bind us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Singapore's approach to maintaining our common space has created room for every community to enjoy our diverse cultural heritage, without asking any specific segment of community to give up its rich inheritances, culture and heritage.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Over time, we have achieved a balance that all communities can accept and it has allowed us to live together in peace for more than half a century.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This approach remains fundamental to tackling racism and racial discrimination, and strengthening racial and religious harmony in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I must stress that we all have a part to play.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: MCCY also works with other Government agencies and community partners to provide opportunities for Singaporeans from diverse backgrounds to have meaningful interactions with one another.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it is not just between Government and people, but also crucially, between people and people as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These include events organised by arts, heritage and sports organisations, the People's Association (PA) and the Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs).

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We also nurture the values of respect and harmony in our students.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Within the classroom, topics on multiculturalism and the importance of racial harmony are taught in subjects like Character and Citizenship Education (CCE), History and Social Studies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Through co-curricular activities and other school experiences, students bond and interact with one another regardless of background.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Learning journeys to cultural and heritage sites and the celebration of cultural festivals also help students foster and develop a stronger sense of identity, learning and also importantly, sensitivity to each other's race and religious issues.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Racial harmony in Singapore is a constant work in progress and our ambition is for the bonds that bind our different communities to grow from strength to strength in the common spaces that we provide.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of us have a part to play in building a nation "regardless of race, language or religion".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We will take the supplementary questions after the political officeholders have addressed the various related questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I call on the next political officeholder who is addressing the next set of questions.
